artists.biography:
Born Betty Mabry in Durham, North Carolina, U.S.A., when she turned sixteen she moved to New York and met several musicians including Jimi Hendrix and Sly Stone. She met Miles Davis in 1967 and married him in 1968. As he stated in his autobiography, in addition to creating turmoil in his personal life, his wife helped him to explore music by introducing him to psychedelic rock guitarist Hendrix and funk innovator Stone.

After the breakup of her marriage, Davis moved to London to pursue her modeling career. She wrote music - a passion since childhood - while in the U.K. and returned to the U.S. with the intention of recording songs with Santana and The Commodores. When those projects didn’t work out, she organised a group of talented West Coast funk musicians and recorded the songs under her own name.

Her first album, Betty Davis, was released in 1973 and her band included members of Sly and the Family Stone, Graham Central Station, The Pointer Sisters, Tower Of Power, and Neil Schon who came from Santana, but went on to form Journey. Davis released two more studio albums: They Say I’m Different (1974) and Nasty Gal (1975). Her backing band, Funkhouse,consisted of her cousin, Larry Johnson on bass, Fred Mills on keyboards, double-platinum artist Carlton Morales on guitar, and Nikki Neal on drums.

perplexity.description:
Released in 1973 through Just Sunshine Records, Betty Davis is the self-titled debut studio album by American funk singer Betty Davis. The album is a bold fusion of hard funk and sweet soul, distinguished by its raw energy, assertive vocals, and eclectic musical arrangements. Produced by Greg Errico of Sly & The Family Stone, the record features contributions from notable musicians such as Neal Schon, Larry Graham, Merl Saunders, Sylvester, and The Pointer Sisters, lending it a dynamic and progressive sound that set it apart from its contemporaries.

Musically, Betty Davis stands as a landmark in funk and soul, showcasing Betty Davis’s fiercely unique artistry and uncompromising vision. The album’s tracks, including standout songs like “If I’m in Luck I Might Get Picked Up” and “Anti Love Song,” blend gritty funk rhythms with psychedelic soul flourishes, reflecting both the era’s musical experimentation and Davis’s singular voice. As the first of her full-length albums, it established her as a pioneering figure in funk, paving the way for her subsequent releases.

Commercially, Betty Davis reached No. 54 on the US Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums chart and No. 202 on the Billboard Bubbling Under the Top LPs chart in 1973. While it did not achieve mainstream pop success, the album earned critical acclaim for its originality and influence, cementing Betty Davis’s reputation as a trailblazer in funk and soul music.
